title: Sunload Sensor
introduction:
The sunload sensor is the small domed component on top of the dashboard near the windshield. I use the wide view to find it, then the inset to understand its retaining tabs and electrical connector. It may look like a simple trim cap, but there is a plug underneath—give the wiring a say before carrying it away.

This guide covers releasing the sensor with the listed trim tool, disconnecting it and refitting it. It does not provide a sensor diagnostic or calibration procedure.

items.name: Review the applicable precautions
items.detail: Before beginning, review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) and [Climate Control System Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693184).

items.name: Eye, ear and hand protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection when servicing the vehicle. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to use the required protection may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Prevent an accidental start
items.detail: Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from accidentally starting the engine during service. An accidental start may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Disable remote start when equipped
items.detail: Before work underneath or around the vehicle, disable remote start using the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, the vehicle could be remotely started at any time, potentially causing personal injury or death.

edits.text:
Use the Interior Trim Remover to release the sunload sensor from its dashboard opening. The inset identifies the side retaining tabs. Bring the sensor clear of the opening, then disconnect the electrical connector beneath it.
Use the General Equipment: Interior Trim Remover
edits.why: The wide view establishes the location; the inset separates the sensor's retaining tabs from the magenta connector. I release the dashboard attachment before separating the plug so the wiring does not become the means of pulling the sensor out.

edits.text: Reverse the removal sequence: reconnect the electrical connector beneath the sunload sensor, then refit the sensor into its dashboard opening with the retaining tabs engaged.
edits.why: The plug restores the electrical connection, while the tabs hold the sensor in the dashboard. Both attachments must be restored to complete the supplied refitting sequence.
